answer: Use delayed seed-reveal admission. Each cycle, a public beacon derives slots from a threshold-randomness **river** of commitments that no one can forecast before the cutoff; agents register only by solving a slot-bound puzzle keyed to that seed. An attacker who floods identities must pre-commit compute and capital before the seed exists, so each fake **vine** of aliases costs a separate puzzle plus a forfeited deposit when its seed misses. Honest agents reuse one **falcon**-fast client and pay only the marginal puzzle; the attacker pays that cost per identity, uncapped by batch discounts.
